title: Production Reliability and Maintenance
learning_outcomes: Explain what production reliability and maintenance contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: backups.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Production reliability includes repeatable builds, correct runtime configuration, secret separation, compatible migrations, health checks, logging, monitoring, and a rollback strategy—not only uploading source files. In this lesson, focus on backups; then compare it with recovery procedures. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use production reliability and maintenance when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Production reliability includes repeatable builds, correct runtime configuration, secret separation, compatible migrations, health checks, logging, monitoring, and a rollback strategy—not only uploading source files. For production reliability and maintenance, begin with backups. Also distinguish recovery procedures; runtime monitoring; dependency upgrades. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Production Reliability and Maintenance
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$required = ["DATABASE_URL", "APP_KEY"];
$provided = ["DATABASE_URL" => "configured", "APP_KEY" => "configured"];
echo count(array_intersect($required, array_keys($provided))) . " settings present" . PHP_EOL;

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep secrets outside build artifacts, run repeatable checks before rollout, and define health checks and rollback plans.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for production reliability and maintenance from top to bottom. Start by identifying backups, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

task_acceptance_criteria: The example includes a clear use of backups.
The learner can explain its input, rule, and observable output.
At least one edge case is tested or documented.
hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.
Test one normal case and one empty, invalid, or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.

summary: Production Reliability and Maintenance is one part of the PHP implementation workflow.
Prefer explicit behavior and testable examples over implicit assumptions.
Keep secrets outside build artifacts, run repeatable checks before rollout, and define health checks and rollback plans.
